 Follow Us On: News Entertainment Music Diljit Dosanjh's Indore show gets clearance hours before concert, 4 songs banned Diljit Dosanjh's Indore show gets clearance hours before concert, 4 songs banned
 Police cleared Diljit Dosanjh's Indore concert hours before the scheduled performance. The approval carries a four-song restriction and extensive security conditions.
 Advertisement Diljit Dosanjh's Indore concert gets police nod with strict security, song curbs. (File Photo-Reuters) By: Dharmendra Kumar Sharma Indore , Nov 15, 2026 18:11 IST Last Updated Nov 15, 2026 18:11 IST Published by Anisha Rao Nov 15, 2026 18:11 IST Diljit Dosanjh's Indore concert will go ahead on November 15, but not without a few restrictions. Police have granted permission for the show just hours before it begins, with organisers instructed to keep four songs off the setlist following objections from the Department of Women and Child Development and references made in the High Court.
 The performance at Delight Dastoor ground on the bypass will also see an extensive security deployment. More than 300 police personnel and over 1,000 volunteers will be on duty as officials prepare for a large turnout. The police have also given written permission for drone surveillance, with watch towers and baggage scanners installed at the venue.
 advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story The four songs were flagged by the Department of Women and Child Development over concerns about their possible impact on children. Following the objections, police directed the organisers not to play the tracks during the concert. The song list includes Patiala Peg , 5 Taara , Case , and Jatt Uthe Fire Karda. 
 Permission for the show had remained uncertain over the past few days , with security arrangements also under scrutiny. Officials have now cleared the event after the organisers completed the required formalities and addressed the conditions laid down by the police.
 Security preparations have been particularly detailed amid reports of threats to the event. Police officials and the organisers discussed around 60 to 70 security points before the final arrangements were put in place. A final inspection of the venue was also scheduled for Saturday.
 The arrangements go beyond the usual checks at a large concert. Attendees will have to undergo security screening, while tickets and passes will be checked strictly at the entry points. The venue will be monitored through drones, and police personnel will be stationed at key locations. A Bomb Detection and Disposal Squad and a strategic security force will also be part of the deployment.
 Organisers have additionally been instructed to ensure proper crowd management, fire and electrical safety, medical facilities and traffic arrangements. With more than 1,000 volunteers assisting the police, the focus will be on managing the expected crowd without compromising security.
 The Indore concert is part of Dosanjh's ongoing AURA India Tour 2026, which began with his Delhi show on October 30 . The singer is set to take the tour to several cities across the country. - Ends ALSO READ | Diljit Dosanjh refuses to play by anyone else's rules. Delhi concert proves it
